failures.criterion: Review finding 4 (the architect's NARROW scope): /v1/replay must not let a caller read every session's inbox
failures.evidence: The session_id token check closes only the session_id '>' route. Any caller of /v1 can register an interest for its own session id in notifications.agent.> or in another session's agent subject (POST /v1/interests/subscribe takes any topic). /v1/replay then answers those subjects with other sessions' stored messages, because replayFollowed accepts every registered topic and CheckFilterSubject allows the wildcard. Live, on a listener and natsd built from this head: A registered notifications.agent.>, and its replay returned 2 messages from notifications.agent.01a17000-bbbb-…; A registered B's agent subject, and its replay returned the same 2 messages. Both plugins already leave every other agent subject out of what they follow (pi-envoy followedSubjects), so the listener can refuse an agent subject other than the session's own, and a wildcard that covers agent subjects, without breaking a caller. Red test: 9f8ac8ffbff6, `cd packages/envoy && go test ./cmd/listener -run TestReplayNeverReturnsAnotherSessionsInboxThroughARegisteredInterest -count=1` -> FAIL: notifications.agent.> returned notifications.agent.ses_other's stored message (seq 1).

observations: A person's removal of a session from an issue, live or replayed, leaves the base subject notifications.dispatch.issue.<KEY> registered and subscribed: Dispatch's removal names only the .> topic. Dispatch publishes issue events on notifications.dispatch.issue.<KEY>.<type>, so the base subject receives nothing from Dispatch. This is existing behaviour, not this change.
